title: Workflow Definition
description: A customer-authored Workflow definition: the document a Platform User writes, a compiler validates, and publication freezes as an immutable version.
$comment: Normative prose: 50-workflows/workflow-dsl.md section 2, which is the specification of this document's shape, and 50-workflows/step-types.md. THIS SCHEMA IS NOT THE VALIDATION AUTHORITY AND CANNOT BE. workflow-dsl.md L9: an unrecognised construct is rejected rather than ignored, and the compiler rejects it, not the schema — R3's must-ignore rule binds consumers of an Orchestra contract, and the compiler is not one but the authority deciding what a definition means. VERSIONING section 6 forbids additionalProperties: false here, so the closure lives where ui-protocol.md CC3 put the same closure for the component catalog: the schema stays open and a compiler pass checks every construct against an allow-list. What this file carries is the shape; what rejects an unknown key is a compiler pass.

name.description: Stable identifier within the Tenant. Never renamed, never reused.
name.$comment: L5 — a definition is retained for the full audit-retention period (W4), so a reused name makes every audit reference to it ambiguous across that period. Identity is this name plus the publication-assigned version, addressed name@version.

version.description: Assigned and frozen by publication, never authored. A draft carries none.
version.$comment: L5 — an author-supplied version would make immutability an authoring convention, since two drafts could claim the same number. Absent from the required list for exactly that reason.

workspace.description: Administrative scope. Never an isolation boundary.

inputs.description: The declared values a Run supplies at admission. MAY be empty.
inputs.$comment: The type notation for an input is NOT decided. workflow-dsl.md section 3 marks the notation in its worked example as illustrative, and section 11 registers the type system with the choice of concrete syntax. This object is deliberately unconstrained rather than given a shape nothing has chosen.

entry.description: The identifier of the Step at which execution begins. MUST name a key of steps.

steps.description: Declared Steps, keyed by author-assigned identifier unique within the version.
steps.$comment: L6 — the identifier is authored, not generated: it is the unit of traceability and the anchor of every diagnostic. Object keys carry that uniqueness.

edges.description: The graph. Control flow lives here and nowhere else.
edges.$comment: L8 — an explicit edge list is more verbose than a next field per Step, and buys a graph analysable without reading any Step body, which is what the reachability, acyclicity and enforcement-point passes need. A condition or parallel Step declares its outcome labels; the edges leaving it carry the targets.

step.description: One declared Step. Every Step declares a type and a Side-Effect Class whatever else it carries.
step.$comment: What each type declares beyond these two is deliberately unconstrained here. The tool object shape, the expression and reference syntax, the predicate on a condition Step and the branch labels leaving it are all notation in workflow-dsl.md's worked example and are explicitly NOT decided — sections 3, 8 and 11 register them, and section 8 is the point at which a definition language would become a programming language. A compiler pass, not this schema, checks a Step body against the allow-list for its type.

type.description: The step type. The set is closed at eight.
type.$comment: step-types.md section 3 — a ninth type is denied by default. Only a tool Step names a Tool to invoke; every other type names none (L7).

side_effect_class.$comment: L6 — a Step with no business effect declares a class too: the class is an input to Policy, never a precondition for evaluation (policy-model.md E3). On a tool Step the declaration is a restatement the compiler checks against the Tool Catalog registration, never an assertion it adopts; a mismatch is rejected. What a declared class constrains on the seven types that reach no Tool of their own is unmade — workflow-dsl.md section 11.

edge.description: One directed edge between two Steps.

branch.description: The outcome label this edge leaves by, on an edge out of a condition or parallel Step.
branch.$comment: The label vocabulary is NOT decided — workflow-dsl.md section 8 registers it with the expression syntax, and the labels in the worked example are notation. Typed as a free string rather than an enum for that reason.

side_effect_class.description: The declared consequence class of a Step or Tool, and a primary input to Policy.
side_effect_class.$comment: GLOSSARY.md, tool-authorization.md. Every Step is evaluated whatever its class (policy-model.md E3): narrowing enforcement by class would leave the platform unable to answer what an Agent read, and would make a declared class a self-issued exemption from the control that reads it.
